one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban characterizes Judge Romeo S. Buenaventura's denial of former Senator Leila de Lima's Motion for Bail Ad Cautelam (in RTC Muntinlupa Branch 256, the third drug-trading case) as 'a big, surprising blow' after over six years' detention. The constitutional rule guarantees bail except for those charged with capital offenses 'WHEN THE EVIDENCE OF GUILT IS STRONG' (CJ supplies the caps). De Lima's motion alleged the prosecution failed to show 'proof evident' of conspiracy, that the evidence was incredible/irrelevant/incompetent and actually supported her innocence and SoJ-duty regularity, that she was not a flight risk, and that humanitarian grounds (longing for family, senior-citizen health issues, life-threatening risks shown by the October 9, 2022 hostage-taking incident) supported release. In a 35-page Order, Buenaventura framed the 'sole issue' as whether the prosecution's evidence was strong, and ruled - after careful review of the totality of evidence - that it was indeed strong, showing prima facie crime and conspiracy. He found De Lima as senior citizen had admitted no serious or life-threatening condition (with expeditious medical furloughs granted), distinguished prior SC cases allowing bail for life/health-injurious detention as not 'obtaining in the instant case,' treated the hostage incident as 'merely an isolated occurrence,' and caveated that 'strong evidence' does not equate to 'proof of guilt beyond reasonable doubt' and does not prejudge the eventual outcome. The Supreme Court's 'unprecedented advisory' last Thursday - to allay public apprehension - assured that 'the denial of bail of De Lima is not the final adjudication of the case.' Panganiban was 'frankly surprised' at the denial given the prior Branch 204 acquittal (Judge Alcantara) on the Rafael Ragos recantation, but a recheck of Buenaventura's decision showed Ragos was NOT among Branch 256 witnesses - so the recantation 'has no effect whatsoever' in this case. He further endorses Buenaventura's credibility latitude, citing that 'the credibility of witnesses is best determined - not by the appellate justices - but by the trial judges' who can observe demeanor, body language, voice timbre, facial twitching, eye movement, and finger fidgeting. De Lima has several remedies - an MR already announced by lawyer Boni Tacardon, followed by higher-court appeals if needed - but these will entail further delay and 'oppressive and detestable detention' in case she is found innocent, which is why court administrator Raul B. Villanueva diligently issued the April 28 memorandum directing nine-month resolution. 'Truly, justice delayed is justice denied. Not just for the accused but also for the prosecution and for the rule of law.'
